unit.sep: Represent directed change,compare geometric and component models,and verify invariants.
unit.careers: Illustrative mapping,design and motion modelling;paper routes are not traffic instructions or professional navigation qualifications.
unit.focus: Magnitude and direction,notation,equivalence,addition,scaling,columns,position,magnitude,midpoints and translations with a declared origin/scale.
unit.phenomenon: Two campus route arrows have equal lengths but point differently;another team mistakes half a displacement for the location of a collection point.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Grid arrows,head-to-tail routes,origin changes,translated shapes and a halfway-point audit.
unit.drivingQuestion: How can a vector model describe a route or design change precisely? KICD: What are vectors? Where are vectors used in real-life situations?
unit.storylineThread: Quantity → notation → equivalent arrows → addition → components → scaling → position → magnitude → midpoint → translation → route application → audit → independent evidence.
unit.coreCompetencies:
Learning to learn: As the learner uses charts and grids to practise addition of vectors.
Self-efficacy: As the learner shares and uses resources from the immediate environment such as plane figures or flip charts to demonstrate equivalent vectors.
unit.values:
Responsibility: As the learner uses resources from the immediate environment such as plane figures, flip charts and relate equivalent vectors.
Unity: As the learner searches and brainstorms on the meaning of the terms vector and scalar quantities and illustrates giving examples.
unit.pcis:
Education for Sustainable Development - Environmental education as learners practice addition of vectors using charts and grids made from resources in the immediate environment.
Road safety: as the learner discusses the meaning of arrows and lines on roads and road signs in relation to movement on the roads to enhance safety.
unit.content: Vector and scalar quantities.; Vector notation; Representation of vectors; Equivalent vectors; Addition of vectors; Multiplication of vectors by scalar; Column vectors; Position vectors; Magnitude of a vector; Midpoint of a vector; Translation vector

sections.title: 1. Quantity,notation and equivalent arrows
sections.prompt: Classify mass5kg and displacement4m west as scalar/vector with a reason. Plot and draw directed AB,CD and BA from VX13. Write AB using arrow notation,a defined bold letter and a vertical column. Decide whether AB and CD are equivalent and explain. Write OB and explain why it differs from AB.
sections.exemplar: Mass scalar:only magnitude/unit;displacement vector:specified magnitude and direction. AB=CD=[4;3]m,equivalent equal changes;BA=[−4;−3]m reverses direction. A defined bold a and arrow-over-AB can name the same vector. OB=[3;5]m is position relative to O,whereas AB starts at A(−1,2). Drawings show listed endpoints,equal axes and arrowheads.

sections.title: 2. Operations and magnitude
sections.prompt: Using VX13,find u+v,−2u and u−v as columns. Show u+v by a head-to-tail drawing from O and compare the endpoint with the component result. Calculate |u−v| with a reasoned formula. Explain the direction and magnitude effect of the negative scalar−2.
sections.exemplar: u+v=[1;2],−2u=[−4;2],u−v=[3;−4]. Head-to-tail O→(2,−1)→(1,2),resultant O→(1,2). Magnitude sqrt(3²+(−4)²)=5m. Negative scalar reverses direction and doubles magnitude,not a negative length.

sections.title: 3. Midpoint and translation
sections.prompt: Find midpoint M of AB by endpoint averages and by A+(1/2)AB;verify AM=MB and distinguish halfAB from OM. Translate triangle PQR by t,plot all three image vertices,and recover t from each matched pair. Compare PQ with P'Q' as a check.
sections.exemplar: M(1,3.5);A+[2;1.5]=(1,3.5),AM=MB=[2;1.5]m. HalfAB is change from A;OM=[1;3.5]m is position. P'(1,−1),Q'(3,−1),R'(2,1);all matched differences[3;−1]m. PQ=P'Q'=[2;0]m;diagram preserves arrow direction,scale and orientation.

sections.title: 4. Use and limits
sections.prompt: Explain one concrete benefit of vector reasoning using a checked result above. Explain why a direction arrow on a road sign alone cannot specify a measured displacement or establish that a route is safe. Name one additional real-route fact needed before acting on a map model.
sections.exemplar: A common translation vector consistently moves all vertices,or a head-to-tail/component check verifies a net movement;accept another specific supported benefit. A sign may convey traffic direction without a quantitative magnitude/scale;obstacles,permissions,crossings/accessibility or current traffic conditions are missing. Paper arithmetic does not justify entering a road or establish practical navigation competence or lasting appreciation.

rubric.excellent: All classifications,notations,arrows,equivalence and position-versus-displacement explanations are correct and clearly linked to origin/scale.
rubric.proficient: Correctly classifies,represents and compares the vectors with valid arrow/column notation and the OB/AB distinction.
rubric.developing: Some correct representations but a direction,notation,equivalence or reference distinction needs correction.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs guided support to connect magnitude,direction,endpoints and column entries.

rubric.excellent: All columns,head-to-tail construction,magnitude setup/result and negative-scalar explanation agree and independently check one another.
rubric.proficient: Correctly adds,scales,subtracts and finds magnitude with an appropriate drawing and sign/direction explanation.
rubric.developing: Some operations are correct but a sign,construction,magnitude formula or negative-scalar interpretation is incomplete.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs guided component or geometric support to carry out and interpret the operations.

rubric.criterion: Locate and verify midpoint and translated images
rubric.excellent: Both midpoint methods,equal halves,reference distinction,all image vertices and recovered shifts/side checks are correct and well justified.
rubric.proficient: Correctly locates the midpoint,distinguishes its position from half-displacement and verifies all translated vertices with a valid side check.
rubric.developing: A valid method is present but a midpoint location,reference,vertex or transformation check needs correction.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs guided support to connect endpoint positions,half-change or a common vertex shift.

rubric.criterion: Explain a practical use and model limit
rubric.excellent: Gives a specific benefit supported by a checked result and clearly distinguishes direction-only signs,quantitative scale and relevant real-route safety/access facts.
rubric.proficient: Explains a supported benefit and a valid limitation/additional fact before using a route model.
rubric.developing: Gives a plausible use but its supporting result or the missing route information is vague or incomplete.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs prompts to relate a vector calculation to a useful decision and its limitations.
